<!-- pr-reviewer: f9f53732200506cf1966758c1fe339c306e68c03 -->
**Needs changes before merge** - the parts-only rule is right and well pinned, but the move of the fit into the app left the setup frame and the kept stock rotation unpinned (two mutations survive). Small test additions, no code change needed.

Scope: the commits after #1539's reviewed head, `git diff 47704e3a f9f53732` (ccfa5a98, b3612bde, and the merge of #1539's head). Stacked on #1539: **merge #1539 first.**

### What looks good
- Moving the logic is exact. With no fixtures, `stock_fit::part_bounds` (via `part_aabb_in` -> `models_aabb_in` -> `facets_in`) gives the same box as the old `solid_aabb_in` path. When the setup has no alignment, `facets_in` falls back to `model::world_facets`, which is the same `facets_of` + `transform_of` + `transform_point` that `model::solid_world_aabb` uses. When it has one, it is the same `models_aabb_in` call. `part_radius_about_in` matches `solid_radius_about_in` in the same way, both aligned and unaligned. The margins, the cylinder centre, the order of the checks (per-side allowance first, then "nothing to fit"), the refusal texts and the kept stock rotation all match the old `State` code line for line. So with no fixtures the `SetStock` is the same for the box, cylinder and per-side fits.
- Layering: `State` no longer does any world-level fit math. `StockFit` / `StockFitSides` just pick a `FitKind`, and `state.rs` lost 48 lines.
- Undo: the GUI and the MCP tool each call `history.execute` once with one `SetStock`, so undo is one step (`the_fit_is_one_undoable_step`).
- Fixtures only -> `"nothing to fit: no models in the document"` (pinned). An empty document gives the same polite status (`shell::stock_fit_without_models_is_a_polite_status`, still green).
- MCP `fit_stock` is chained in `mcp/tools.rs` and calls the same `fit_command`. It refuses a bad `shape`, `sides` together with a cylinder, and a non-finite or wrong-length `sides` by name.
- G54 anchor: `anchor_reference` reads `part_bounds(active)`. The existing `model_bounds_anchors_follow_the_aligned_part` still pins its frame: when I dropped the frame inside `part_bounds`, it failed.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code. Both new modules carry provenance. The decision file, the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1538` are there, and the commit subjects are conventional. No process files, `PROCESS_VERSION`, snapshots, goldens, build.rs, `.github` or dependencies are touched.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream/main, clean; macOS, debug, sccache)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app lib | 194 passed |
| app `stock_fit_fixtures` | 6 passed |
| app `heights_fixtures` | 8 passed |
| app `setup_align` | 10 passed |
| app `mcp` | 22 passed |
| app `fixture_locate_stock`, `mcp_vise`, `mcp_workholding`, `mcp_setup`, `mcp_plate`, `mcp_accessory`, `stock_source_verdict` | 3 / 1 / 1 / 9 / 1 / 2 / 22 passed |
| ui lib (CWD `crates/ui`, `--test-threads=1`) | 732 passed, 5 ignored |
| ui `shell`, `fixtures`, `models`, `operations` | 21 / 7 / 4 / 31 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Mutation check
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `part_bounds` back to `solid_aabb_in` (fit reads every model) | red: 5 `stock_fit_fixtures` tests, `shell::stock_fit_with_a_vise...`, strip pin, anchor pin |
| `part_radius_about_in` keeps fixtures | red: cylinder, every-kind, MCP and shell pins |
| strip (`stock_info`) back to `solid_aabb_in` | red: `the_readout_is_the_parts_never_the_vise` |
| anchor (`anchor_reference`) back to `solid_aabb_in` | red: `model_bounds_anchors_are_the_parts_never_the_vise` |
| MCP `fit_stock` bypasses `fit_command` with `solid_aabb_in` + `fit_box` | red: `mcp_fit_stock_with_a_vise_gives_the_part_box` |
| frame dropped in `part_bounds` (every reader) | red only through `setup_align_tests::model_bounds_anchors_follow_the_aligned_part`: no fit test fails |
| **frame dropped in `fit_command` (`fitted(world, <no setup>, kind)`)** | **survives**: all of `stock_fit_fixtures`, `setup_align`, ui lib (732), `shell`, `fixtures`, `models` green |
| **frame dropped in the cylinder radius only (`part_radius_about_in`)** | **survives** |
| **kept rotation dropped (`rot` -> identity in `fit_command`)** | **survives** |

(Passing `None` for the setup is an equivalent mutant, since `None` resolves to the active setup. To drop the frame I named a setup that does not exist.)

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the fit in an aligned setup.** `crates/app/src/stock_fit.rs:76` (`fitted(world, active.as_deref(), kind)`) and `:64` (the radius call) can lose the setup frame and no test notices. The PR now owns the fit, and #326's "the stock is square to the setup frame" is a stock-placement claim: a wrong frame here moves the stock that every height and the sim read. Please add a test to `stock_fit_fixtures`, for example a 40 x 20 x 8 part (off-centre in X/Y) with a vise, the setup aligned to a quarter turn and a flip (`AlignPart` / the app's alignment command). It should assert that the box fit, the cylinder fit and the per-side fit give the turned part's box (20 x 40 footprint) plus the margin, and that the result equals the fit of the same aligned part without the vise. Then check that dropping the frame in `fitted` and in `part_radius_about_in` turns it red.
2. **Pin the kept stock rotation.** `crates/app/src/stock_fit.rs:77-80` keeps the stock's deliberate rotation, but replacing it with identity leaves every test green. One assertion fixes this: set a stock with a non-identity `rot` before the fit, then check that the fitted stock's `transform_of(...).rot` is unchanged. It can go in the test above or in `the_fit_is_one_undoable_step`.
3. **File the skill-row follow-up.** The PR body says the `camcraft-mcp` skill row for `fit_stock` waits for a process PR, but I found no issue for it (search `fit_stock`: none). Please file `MCP: camcraft-mcp skill row for fit_stock` (`P5`, `effort:low`, `area:mcp`, `source:agent`, like #1343 / #1337) and name it in the PR body. AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool" accepts a follow-up only when it is filed and named.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- A negative `margin` over MCP (`fit_stock {"margin": -1}`) is refused as `stock fit refused: models have no usable extent` (from `fit_measures`). That message does not name the margin, although the tool description says a negative allowance is "refused by name". A `margin >= 0 && finite` check in `stock_fit::fitted`, with the same wording as the per-side check, would fix both surfaces. The GUI has always shown that message, so this is fine as a `P7` follow-up.
- With fixtures only, the refusal reads "no models in the document" while the tree shows a vise. Something like "no part models to fit (fixtures are not measured)" would be clearer. This is polish.
- `mcp_fit_stock_with_a_vise_gives_the_part_box` ends with an `undo` but asserts nothing after it. Asserting that the stock is back to the 54 x 54 x 10 fit (or the cylinder) would make it the MCP undo pin.
- `crates/app/src/lib.rs:116`: `pub mod stock_fit;` is the only module there without its one-line `// #N:` note.
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs` is 1794 lines (+1 here). This is pre-existing, and the PR moves the other way overall (`state.rs` -48).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
